questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Zagreb?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Croatia is Zagreb.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Croatia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Croatia article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Zagreb.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Croatia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Croatia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Croatia about 56,594 square kilometres; Moldova about 33,844 square kilometres; North Macedonia about 25,713 square kilometres; Montenegro about 13,883 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Croatia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Croatia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Croatia article.

questions.proof: Croatia is in Central and Southeast Europe, bordering Hungary to the northeast, Serbia to the east, Bosnia and Herzegovina to the south-east, Montenegro to the south-east, the Adriatic Sea to the south-west and Slovenia to the northwest.
